sections.h2: Where is Coeur d'Alene and what is the city built around?
sections.html:
Coeur d'Alene is the county seat of Kootenai County and the most populous city in North Idaho. It sits on the north shore of Lake Coeur d'Alene, which is 25 miles long, about 30 miles east of Spokane, Washington, and west of the Coeur d'Alene Mountains. Locals call it the Lake City or CDA.

The city began as a fort town: General William Tecumseh Sherman sited Fort Sherman on the lake in 1878. The Northern Pacific Railroad reached the town in 1883, and miners and timber workers followed. The town was incorporated in 1887 and the city in 1906, on September 4. The 2020 census counted 54,628 residents, and the Census Bureau estimated 58,179 on July 1, 2025.

Downtown is organized around the lake. The Coeur d'Alene Resort, with its 3,300-foot floating boardwalk, the 165-acre Tubbs Hill natural area, City Park and Beach, and McEuen Park all sit along the waterfront. A seller whose house is within a short walk of that area sells a different product than one on the edge of town, and the listing photos and description should say which it is.

  • Founded 1878, incorporated as a city September 4, 1906
  • Elevation: 2,247 feet
  • Lake length: 25 miles
  • Estimated population on July 1, 2025: 58,179 (Census Bureau)

sections.h2: How does Coeur d'Alene earn its living?
sections.html:
Coeur d'Alene started with mining and logging, and tourism has been the main influence on the local economy since the 1980s. The city is also the health care, education, media, manufacturing and retail center for North Idaho. Hecla Mining is headquartered in the city, and Kootenai Health is the largest employer in Kootenai County.

The Coeur d'Alene School District, with about 11,000 students in 18 schools, is the sixth largest in Idaho and the second largest employer in the county. North Idaho College, founded in 1933 on the former site of Fort Sherman, enrolls more than 5,000 students.

Wikipedia notes that the city has grown significantly since the 1990s, partly through tourism and partly through people moving in from other western states. Whether you bought long ago or recently, compare your loan payoff with a realistic net before you accept any offer.

sections.h2: What do Coeur d'Alene's winters and summers mean for a house?
sections.html:
A house in Coeur d'Alene has to cope with cold winters as well as warm summer days. The average daily temperature is 31.2 degrees Fahrenheit in January and December and 70.1 degrees in July. Temperatures pass 90 degrees on about 18.3 days a year, and there may be several nights below 10 degrees. Average annual rainfall is about 25 inches.

Those figures translate into a short checklist for sellers:

  • Roof condition and attic insulation, since winter weather is hardest on older roofs
  • Furnace or heat pump age, which a buyer's inspector will test
  • Gutters, downspouts and drainage near the foundation after snowmelt
  • Decks and docks, which take the heaviest weather exposure on lakefront lots

A house whose roof or heating system has not been checked in years can run into trouble at a buyer's inspection. A cash buyer looks at the same items but accepts the house as-is and builds the repair cost into the offer.

sections.h2: How does wildfire risk figure into selling a North Idaho house?
sections.html:
Wildfire is a real consideration for houses near forest, and Idaho runs a state program to fight it. The Idaho Department of Lands protects 9 million acres of forest and rangeland from wildfire, with a Coeur d'Alene office at 3284 W. Industrial Loop, and it educates the public about defensible space as part of its prevention work.

The department also publishes a fire restrictions finder. It warns that state and county regulations and penalties apply, and that a person who violates a restriction and starts a wildfire is liable for suppression costs, including damage to property and resources.

If your property backs onto forest, clearing brush and dead material around the house before showings helps a buyer feel at ease. These pages do not set a city rule for Coeur d'Alene, so check with the city and your insurer about requirements that apply to your lot.

sections.h2: Do short-term rentals transfer to a new owner in Coeur d'Alene?
sections.html:
No. Under section 17.08.1030 of the Coeur d'Alene city code, a short-term rental permit is non-transferable and valid only for the residential dwelling named in the application. If the dwelling is sold or title is otherwise transferred, the permit automatically expires on the transfer of title.

That rule matters if your house has been an income property near the lake. A buyer cannot inherit your permit, so any buyer who wants to run a short-term rental has to apply on their own. Idaho law also limits what cities can do: Senate Bill 1162 of 2025 amended section 67-6539 of the Idaho Code so that a city or county may not adopt or enforce an ordinance that has the express or practical effect of prohibiting short-term rentals.

If you plan to sell, tell buyers plainly that the permit ends at closing. A buyer who wanted the booking income will price the house differently from a buyer who wants a full-time home. Keep the permit number, booking history and any tax filings handy.

sections.h2: How does Kootenai County handle property tax and exemptions?
sections.html:
Kootenai County collects the property tax on Coeur d'Alene houses, with the first half due on or before December 20 and the second half due on or before June 20 of the next year. Tax notices are mailed annually by the fourth Monday in November.

The county explains that a homeowner's exemption reduces the assessed value of a primary residence by half its value, up to $125,000 beginning in 2021. The Property Tax Reduction Program accepts applications only between January 1 and April 15, and the benefit must be applied for and qualified for each year. The Idaho State Tax Commission says you may appeal your assessed value to the county Board of Equalization by the fourth Monday in June, and a further appeal goes to the State Board of Tax Appeals or district court within 30 days.

If you sold your primary residence, ask the closing agent how the year's tax was divided and whether the exemption on your old house will continue under the new owner. Keep your own copy of the final settlement statement.

sections.h2: What disclosure does a Coeur d'Alene seller have to make?
sections.html:
Most Idaho residential sellers must complete a property condition disclosure form. Section 55-2504 of the Idaho Code covers any person who intends to transfer residential real property, including non-owner-occupied rental property, and requires them to complete the form prescribed in section 55-2508.

Section 55-2505 lists exemptions. These include transfers by a fiduciary in an estate, guardianship, conservatorship or trust, foreclosure transfers, transfers to a spouse or lineal relative, and a transfer by someone who got the house by inheritance and has not lived there in the last year. Section 55-2509 then requires the buyer to sign and return the form when one applies. If the house was never your primary residence, ask your closing agent which category applies.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale fit a Coeur d'Alene house?
sections.html:
A cash sale fits when the owner wants speed and certainty more than a long marketing period. Situations we see in North Idaho include:

  • An inherited house or cabin that no heir plans to keep
  • A house with an older roof or heating system that would fail a buyer's inspection
  • A former short-term rental whose permit ends at closing
  • A move for work or family that sets a firm closing date

Cash Home Buyers buys as-is, with no commissions and no closing costs charged to you by us, and you owe nothing if you decline. Because every house and every payoff is different, compare an offer with the net from a listing before you decide.

faqs.q: What county is Coeur d'Alene in?
faqs.a: Coeur d'Alene is the county seat of Kootenai County, Idaho.

faqs.q: When are Kootenai County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due on or before December 20 and the second half on or before June 20 of the following year. Notices are mailed by the fourth Monday in November.

faqs.q: Does a short-term rental permit transfer when I sell my Coeur d'Alene house?
faqs.a: No. The city code says the permit is non-transferable and expires automatically when title transfers, so the buyer must apply for a new one.

faqs.q: Is there a homeowner's exemption in Kootenai County?
faqs.a: Yes. Kootenai County says the exemption reduces a primary residence's assessed value by half, up to $125,000, beginning in 2021.

faqs.q: How far is Coeur d'Alene from Spokane?
faqs.a: About 30 miles. The two cities form a combined statistical area that crosses the Idaho and Washington border.
